subject: Private VPC deployment: sequencing and orchestration for control/data plane handoff
thread_text:
From: NimbusCloud Infra <infra@nimcloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC deployment: control/data sequencing and handoff

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the scoping call last week. We are lining up the on-prem cutover window for our Private VPC and need a short, ordered sequencing document for the control-plane / data-plane handoff so our SREs and colo team can coordinate cages and BGP prep.

Primary asks:
- One-page sequencing with explicit dependencies (who touches what, expected IP/VIP changes)
- Canary plan and rollback triggers (15-30 minute window preferred)
- Any temporary routing or NAT changes required on our edge before traffic shift

Can you share an initial sequencing draft by EOD Monday so we can align internal approvers? Attaching the topo we discussed.

Attachment: nimbus-topo-20250820.svg (topology diagram stub)

Thanks,
Rahul Menon
Infra Lead, NimbusCloud
infra@nimcloud.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: NimbusCloud Infra <infra@nimcloud.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2025 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment: control/data sequencing and handoff

Hi Rahul —

Thanks, this is helpful. Attached is a short sequencing sketch (also pasted below) that maps control-plane activities (certificate exchange, API endpoint propagation, control-plane VIP failover) and data-plane (NAT, BGP announcement cutover, service adjacency). It focuses on minimizing the blast radius during the window and keeping an automated rollback path.

High-level sequencing (initial draft) — order of operations:
1) Pre-checks (T-72h): confirm colocation fiber, ASN/BGP prep, KMS access and audit keys, NTPS synced
2) Control plane readiness (T-4h): exchange signed certs, provision control-plane endpoints behind provisional VIPs, test API auth (smoke), configure RBAC for on-prem ops users
3) Canary deploy (T-1h): route 1% of traffic to new data-plane; validate latency and KV-cache behavior for long-context requests
4) Full data-plane cut (T+0): change BGP announcements to new on-prem edge, enable NAT rules, verify egress paths and telemetry
5) Post-cut health checks (T+15m / T+60m): token-level traces, top-5 API SLOs, KV cache hitrate, per-model latencies
6) Rollback (if any critical SLO breached within the canary window): revert BGP to prior ASN, disable new NAT, demote control-plane VIP to maintenance mode

Attachments: 20250824-control-data-seq.pdf (sequencing and dependency matrix)

Open questions for Nimbus team:
- Can you confirm the ASN and whether the colo supports 2-way BFD?
- Do you require a dedicated peering VLAN or can we reuse the existing 10G crossconnect?

Next step: can Jonas and Irene confirm the operational commands we expect to run (BGP withdraw/announce sequence, VIP flip script) and I’ll consolidate into a single runbook.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Deployments — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, NimbusCloud Infra <infra@nimcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2025 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment: control/data sequencing and handoff

Marissa, Rahul — quick technical clarifications and an ops note. I reviewed the topo and Marissa’s sequencing. A few specifics we should lock before final runbook:

- Control-plane endpoints: we will provision three control-plane VMs behind a floating VIP with active/passive failover. The VIP will sit in the 192.168.254.0/29 range (proposal) and be announced locally. We will avoid propagating the VIP to Nimbus BGP until the canary stage; initial testing uses direct host routes from the colo jump hosts.
- API cert exchange: we require CSR signatures for the on-prem CA; please provide the CA fingerprint ahead of T-4h.
- BGP sequence (recommended):
   1) Advertise community no-export for tentative edge (so it doesn’t leak to transit)
   2) Announce the new prefixes with local pref lower than production during canary (so only controlled ASNs prefer it)
   3) After green canary, increase local-pref on the Nimbus-facing session and withdraw the old prefixes
- BFD: if Nimbus supports 2-way BFD we can get a faster failover (sub-second); if not, extend probes intervals and tighten health checks.

I uploaded a quick endpoint sheet with expected VIPs and the announce plan — controlplane-endpoints.xlsx

Operational commands I’ll run during the window (high level):
- ip route add/flush host routes for VIPs on jump hosts
- bgp session adjust: set local-pref attribute via route-maps, add/remove community tags
- health checks: curl + prom-based synthetic checks against /healthz endpoints

Marissa: I’ll slot time in our runbook draft for Tessa to own the post-cut observability checks.

—Jonas
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment: sequencing and orchestration for control/data plane handoff

Adding the ops checklist and canary acceptance criteria. I recommend a two-tier canary: 1% baseline traffic for 30 minutes, then 10% for an additional 30 minutes before full flip. If at any step latency p50 increases > 40% or error rate > 0.5% for the prom-slo-indexed endpoints, we trigger rollback.

Quick checklist excerpt (ops):
- Preflight (T-72h): KMS access verified, JIT jump host keys provisioned, VLAN and BGP session configs committed in colo portal
- T-4h: CSR signed and certs staged on control-plane nodes, VIP allocated but not announced via BGP
- T-1h (canary start): enable partial routing, configure traffic-splitting via ingress rules, create monitoring dashboard (Tessa)
- T+0 (full flip): announce prefixes at local-pref=200, withdraw legacy with local-pref=100
- Post (T+15m): validate telemetry; T+60m: final acceptance and update runbook

Attachment: canary-plan.md (markdown stub with acceptance thresholds and Prom queries)

Irene Choi
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

We’ve reviewed the sequencing PDF and the canary plan; primary ask on our side: include an explicit NOC escalation contact and the exact CLI snippets for rollback (jonas’s high-level commands are perfect; a paste-ready script will reduce human error).

Marta Lopez
